items.title: Keith Ingham interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: as well as accompanying and arranging for Peggy Lee and Maxine Sullivan

ctx.x: Pianist Keith Ingham has come a long way since the days he had to sneak jazz recordings into his London home. Born in 1942, he displayed a talent for foreign languages, excelling in French, Italian and Chinese. He augmented his classical piano studies with constant listening to jazz recordings from the States, eventually teaching himself to play jazz piano. Keith accompanied visiting and emigrating American jazz artists, including Benny Carter and Ben Webster, and recorded his first album as a leader with Bud…
Keith was interviewed on September 12, 1997 in Chautauqua, New York by Monk Rowe, Director of the Hamilton College Jazz Archive.
